replies.author: MasterProX
replies.body:
My understanding is that the original poster suggests for staff to treat rudeness and disrespect with more gravity, akin to how infractions for hacking are allocated. I'm assuming that the difference in ramifications — most often warns and kicks for harassment, and temporary and permanent bans for hacking — is giving the (misleading) appearance of the latter being addressed more seriously than the former, though ultimately almost every punishment depends heavily on the situation and context...

In other words, this thread is pertinent to bullying more so than hacking (which is almost irrelevant entirely); all that's being proposed is for staff members to exercise minimal — or, at least, less — leniency with players being intrusive and discourteous to others, because few can truly foresee the scope of such actions.

replies.author: MasterProX
replies.body:
Yes, that's a given — the flames of hatred are ubiquitous and you cannot fully extinguish them. You can, however, strive to efface as much of them as possible, the same way a violinist can never truly transcend to "perfection" but nonetheless devotes his life to becoming as "perfect" as humanly possible. The same can be said about moderators; although it is impossible for them to forge a utopian community devoid of negativity, they can surely try their best. In the end, that's their responsibility, no? To uphold the highest feasible level of order, thus distinguishing Avicus from the "riskier" corners of the Internet?

On the server, it's commonplace for me to see players attacking one another with reproachful epithets and contemptuous appellations, with little being done to combat this — if a staff member is present at all, far too many verbal warnings are given, and a kick is only issued when the reprehensible player(s) in question start talking back to the staff when simply an official warning and a subsequent kick, if necessary, would suffice (the same result but with greater stricture, in effect the whole purpose of this thread). This prolongs the bad sentiment and sets a poor example, among other repercussions.

I'm not implying that bans should be more liberally doled out to anyone exhibiting any level of disrespect (way too extremist), but a lot of people do seem to underestimate the potential power of one message...
